title: The Lost Lantern
author: GamebookRuntime
intro:
The village elder did not choose you. He had no one left to choose. The lantern went dark somewhere on the forest road, and since then the wolves have been bolder, the shrine keeper colder, and the river on the wrong side of the argument.

You have one night, one promise, and a road that splits in two.

*What the light was for, nobody says out loud.*

spirits-riddle.name: The spirits' riddle
spirits-riddle.description: “Six paths I show, only chance decides.”

keepers-words.name: The keeper's words
keepers-words.description: “It was never about delivering the light.”

start.text:
# The Lost Lantern

The forest road swallowed the last light of the sun an hour ago. Your lantern — the one you promised the village elder you would deliver to the shrine on the hill — has gone dark.

Somewhere ahead, a wolf howls. Somewhere behind, the village lights flicker. You hold the cold lantern tight and make a choice.

options.text: Push on through the dark forest toward the shrine.
Turn back to the village and admit defeat.
Take the long way round and pass the man in the dark coat.

forest.text:
## Into the Dark

The trees lean close like old conspirators. After a while you reach a fork where a crooked signpost points two ways: *left, toward running water*, and *right, toward a faint warm glow*.

Your grandmother's words come back to you: *"Wolves fear fire, but water remembers names."*

options.text: Follow the sound of running water.
Slip back to the village market square.

wanderer.text:
## The One Who Knows

A man in a dark coat is waiting where the path forks, as if he had been there before you. He does not give his name and does not say hello. He only says: *"I know what the light was for. Ask me one thing — but one thing only."*

options.text: "What was the light for?" — you take his answer with you.
Ask for nothing. Walk past him.

camp.text:
## The Warm Glow

The glow belongs to a small campfire, and beside it sits a traveller roasting chestnuts. She waves you closer without a word.

*"The shrine keeper sent me,"* she says, handing you a **small flask of lantern oil**. "The wolves fear fire. Walk, don't run."

When you look up from the flask, she is gone — only warm ashes remain.

options.text: Thank the fire and climb to the shrine.
Search the ashes for a clue.
